A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a simple, low-cost ball-drop impact tester with a software-hardware interface for conducting programmable electric field assisted impact experiments on various materials.
this set-up would be useful for studying the shock absorption capability of small-sized smart materials and structures under impact loading.
the proposed set-up is capable of providing a simple, fast, and inexpensive method for investigating the mechanical properties of small-sized systems and smart structures under impact conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developed system can be used to study the shock absorption capability of a variety of small-sized materials and structures under programmable electric fields.
the developed system is a simple and cost-effective way to conduct dynamic experiments on small-sized systems under controlled electric field.
the developed ball-drop impact tester provides a unique platform to investigate the dynamic behavior of materials and systems that are sensitive to electric field.
